- Streaming NLP pipeline with multilingual encoder

## Code Example
```python
# Skeleton: dataflow for streaming NLP pipeline
def process_message(msg):
    pre = preprocess(msg)  # tokenize, remove PII, handle emojis
    vec = encoder.encode(pre.text, lang=pre.lang)
    score_sent = sentiment_head(vec)
    score_topic = topic_head(vec)
    score_policy = policy_head(vec, pre.code_blocks)
    final = fuse([score_sent, score_topic, score_policy])
    return final
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests on-device NLP design, privacy guarantees, and multilingual handling with code-switching in a beginner-friendly setting. Assesses ability to blend regex-based detection with a compact NER model and plan labeling, rollout, and evaluation.

## Key Concepts

- On-device inference with WebAssembly
- PII detection: regex patterns + lightweight NER
- Multilingual and code-switching resilience
- Privacy guarantees and staged rollout
- Evaluation metrics: precision/recall for redactions

## Code Example

```javascript
function redactPII(text) {
  const email = /\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b/g;
  const phone = /\b(\+?\d{1,3}[-.\s+]?)?(\(?\d{2,4}\)?[-.\s+]?\d{3,4}[-.\s+]?\d{3,4})\b/g;
  return text
    .replace(email, "[REDACTED_EMAIL]")
    .replace(phone, "[REDACTED_PHONE]");
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend to additional languages?
- How would you validate redaction quality without leaking data?

## Code Example

```python
# Pseudocode: simple risk score from keyword regexes per language
import re
from typing import List

class Detector:
    def __init__(self, patterns: List[str]):
        self.regexes = [re.compile(p) for p in patterns]
    def score(self, text: str) -> float:
        return sum(bool(r.search(text)) for r in self.regexes) / len(self.regexes)
```
